perf.summary: Rank computes an entire first block (the 'pow' loop and the loop that accumulates into 'r') whose results r and the per-iteration pow are never used; only the second Horner loop's 'result' is returned. This is dead, expensive work including a ModPow.
perf.currentCost: First loop: n-2 mults to build pow. Second loop: n-2 iterations each doing a ModPow on i==0 (~30 mod-mults) or a modular division pow/n (integer division on longs, NOT modular inverse) and accumulating into unused r. All discarded.
perf.proposedChange: Delete the first 'pow' loop and the first accumulation loop entirely; keep only the final Horner evaluation that fills 'result'. The function reduces to: long result=0,pn=1; for(int i=n-3;i>=0;i--){result=(result+(long)seq[i]*pn)%MOD; pn=pn*n%MOD;} return result;
perf.rationale: Removes ~2*(n-2) iterations plus a ModPow that produce values never returned, cutting work roughly in half and eliminating a misleading non-modular 'pow / n' division. The returned value is unchanged.
perf.risk: Confirmed dead: r is local and never returned; the only return path uses 'result'. Pure removal, identical observable output. (Note the deleted code also contained a latent bug—pow/n is not modular—so removing it is strictly safe and clarifying.)
